title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.
key_points: Prediabetes means blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet diabetic — a key window to act.
Losing a modest amount of weight and staying active can sharply cut the risk of progressing.
Around 150 minutes of activity a week plus healthier eating is the core of prevention.
Many people with prediabetes don't know they have it, so screening matters.
content_html: Type 2 diabetes rarely appears overnight. For most people it's preceded by years of prediabetes — and that gap is exactly where prevention works.
extra_html: The CDC explains that prediabetes is a state where blood sugar is elevated but not high enough to be diabetes, and that it's both common and often unnoticed — many people have it without knowing. The encouraging news is what happens when it's caught. Evidence from the CDC's National Diabetes Prevention Program shows that losing a modest amount of body weight (around 5–7%) and getting about 150 minutes of physical activity a week can cut the risk of developing type 2 diabetes substantially. The recipe is unglamorous but real: more movement, healthier eating with less added sugar and refined carbohydrate, and steady progress rather than crash dieting. Because prediabetes is silent, a simple blood test at a checkup is how most people learn they're in that window — in time to do something about it.

source.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Understanding Blood Pressure
related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

related.title: Building a Balanced Plate
related.hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.

related.title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
related.hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

related.title: Reversing Prediabetes Pays Off for the Heart
related.hook: Prediabetes isn't a one-way street. People who brought their blood sugar back to normal cut their risk of dying from heart disease or being hospitalized for heart failure by 58%.

flashcards.prompt: What is prediabetes, and why does it matter?
flashcards.back_html: Blood sugar that's higher than normal but not yet diabetic. It's a crucial window — lifestyle changes at this stage can prevent or delay full type 2 diabetes.

flashcards.prompt: What does the CDC say most effectively lowers the risk of type 2 diabetes?

choices.text: Modest weight loss and regular physical activity
A single medication with no other changes

flashcards.explanation_html: The CDC's prevention programs show that losing a modest amount of weight and getting about 150 minutes of activity a week substantially reduce the risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.
